questions.q: A customer in Onitsha uses a mobile banking app on her smartphone to pay an online fashion store for a dress. This transaction is best described as
questions.explanation: Mobile commerce is e-commerce carried out through mobile devices such as smartphones. It is not business-to-business e-commerce because a consumer is buying from a business, and electronic data interchange refers to computer-to-computer exchange of business documents between organisations.

questions.q: A bottled water company in Makurdi decides to reach customers in remote villages through wholesalers and small retailers instead of selling only at its factory. This decision relates mainly to which element of the marketing mix?
questions.explanation: Place covers distribution channels, warehousing, transportation and retail locations that ensure a product reaches customers conveniently. Price concerns the amount charged, product concerns the goods or services offered, and promotion covers communication with customers.

questions.q: The reward received by an entrepreneur for organising the other factors of production and bearing business risk is
questions.explanation: Entrepreneurship is rewarded with profit, which is the residual income left after costs have been paid and may be negative if the business makes a loss. Labour earns wages or salaries, capital earns interest, and land earns rent.

questions.q: When a trader in Aba agrees to accept payment for goods three months after delivery, the function of money that makes such postponed payment possible is money as
questions.explanation: A standard of deferred payment allows credit transactions to be settled in the future. A medium of exchange would apply if payment were made immediately, while a unit of account is mainly used to quote prices and a store of value is about keeping purchasing power over time.

questions.q: In an online shop, the feature that allows a customer to select goods and keep them temporarily before checking out is called
questions.explanation: A shopping cart, also called a basket, holds items selected by a customer before checkout. A payment gateway processes payments, an escrow account holds funds until agreed conditions are met, and a domain name is the website address.

questions.q: Musa, a trader in Kano, wants to increase sales quickly by offering customers a free bar of soap for every two bars bought during Ramadan. This practice is best described as
questions.explanation: A short-term incentive such as buy-two-get-one-free is sales promotion aimed at stimulating immediate purchases. Personal selling involves direct persuasion by a salesperson, while public relations and publicity are mainly about building image or gaining unpaid media attention.

questions.q: A firm in Ota replaces some manual assembly work with automated machines, so that each worker now uses more equipment to produce a larger output. This method of production is described as
questions.explanation: Capital-intensive production uses a relatively high proportion of machinery and equipment compared with labour. Labour-intensive production relies more on workers, subsistence production is mainly for personal or family consumption, and direct production is production by an individual for their own use.

questions.q: A commercial bank receives a new deposit of ₦200,000. If the cash reserve ratio is 10%, what is the maximum additional loans that the banking system can create from the deposit?
questions.explanation: Required reserve is ₦20,000, so excess reserves are ₦180,000. The credit multiplier is 1 ÷ 0.10 = 10, and maximum additional loans equal ₦180,000 × 10 = ₦1,800,000. The amount ₦2,000,000 is the increase in total deposits including the original deposit, not the additional loans.

questions.q: Which of the following activities is a tertiary occupation?
questions.explanation: Tertiary occupations provide services rather than extracting raw materials or manufacturing goods, so banking is a service activity. Cassava farming is primary, while fish smoking and shoe manufacturing are secondary activities because they process or transform raw materials into finished or semi-finished products.

questions.q: A Nigerian exporter in Lagos sells vegetable oil to a buyer in Accra on FOB Lagos terms. Under the contract, which cost is borne by the buyer?
options: Ocean freight from Lagos to Accra and marine insurance
Loading the goods on board the vessel at Lagos
Export documentation and customs clearance at Lagos port
Transporting the goods from the exporter's warehouse to Lagos port
questions.explanation: Under FOB, the seller's duty ends once the goods have been placed on board the vessel at the named port. The buyer therefore bears the main carriage and marine insurance. Loading, pre-shipment transport and export clearance at Lagos are obligations on the seller's side.

questions.q: A Nigerian bank in Lagos earns a commission by confirming a letter of credit for a customer in Ghana. In Nigeria's balance of payments, this earning is classified as
questions.explanation: A commission earned from a foreign customer for a banking service is payment for a service sold abroad, so it is an invisible export. Visible exports are physical goods, while invisible imports are services bought from abroad. A capital inflow relates mainly to investment or loan flows, not service income.

questions.q: Which of the following transactions is recorded as a debit item in Nigeria's balance of payments?
options: Freight earned by a Nigerian shipping company on goods carried to Ghana
Proceeds from cashew nuts exported to India
Payment for tractors imported from China
Insurance premium received from a foreign client by a Nigerian insurer
questions.explanation: A debit entry records payments made to foreigners or imports of goods and services. Payment for imported tractors represents money leaving Nigeria and is therefore a debit. Export proceeds and service income received from abroad are credits.

questions.q: After paying a motorist's accident claim, an insurer takes over the motorist's right to recover the amount from the negligent driver who caused the accident. Which principle of insurance is illustrated?
questions.explanation: Subrogation is the insurer's right, after indemnifying the insured, to stand in the insured's place and recover the loss from the responsible third party. Contribution concerns sharing a loss among insurers covering the same risk, while utmost good faith concerns full disclosure of material facts.

questions.q: Ngozi insured the same stock against fire with two different insurance companies. When fire occurred, the insurers shared the loss between them so that Ngozi would not recover more than the value of the stock. Which principle of insurance is involved?
questions.explanation: Contribution requires insurers that cover the same risk to share the loss so that the insured is not over-compensated. The average clause instead applies where the sum insured is less than the actual value, while subrogation concerns recovery from a third party.

questions.q: A group of promoters in Aba wants to register a limited liability company. Which document states the proposed company's name, registered office, objects and share capital?
questions.explanation: The memorandum of association is the external charter that states the company's name, registered office, objects and share capital. The articles of association regulate internal management, while the certificate of incorporation is issued after the company has been registered.

questions.q: In a partnership in Ibadan, one partner contributes capital but by agreement takes no part in managing the business. Such a partner is best described as a
questions.explanation: A sleeping or dormant partner contributes capital but does not participate in management. An active partner manages the business, while a nominal partner merely lends a name without contributing capital.

questions.q: A public corporation such as a state water board is established mainly to
options: Provide an essential service to the public, often without the primary aim of maximizing profit
Limit the personal liability of its two to fifty shareholders
Raise capital by selling shares to the general public
Share profits among members according to their purchases
questions.explanation: A public corporation is a statutory body set up by government mainly to provide essential goods or services rather than to distribute profit to shareholders. The other descriptions describe a cooperative society, a public limited company and a private limited company rather than a public corporation.

questions.q: Which body is mainly responsible for regulating the Nigerian capital market and approving the issue of securities to the public?
questions.explanation: The Securities and Exchange Commission is the apex regulator of the Nigerian capital market and approves securities issued to the public. The Nigerian Exchange Group operates the trading platform, while the Central Bank and NDIC focus mainly on banking and deposit protection.

questions.q: The market price of a quoted share is ₦23. An investor instructs a stockbroker to buy the shares only if the price falls to ₦18 or lower. This instruction is a
questions.explanation: A buy limit order sets the highest price at which the investor is willing to buy, so the broker buys only at that price or lower. A market order is executed immediately, and an odd-lot order concerns quantity rather than a price condition.

questions.q: A wholesaler in Aba bought 400 cartons of soap at ₦2,500 per carton and sold all of them at ₦3,000 per carton less a trade discount of 5%. What was the wholesaler's gross profit?
questions.explanation: The net selling price per carton is ₦3,000 less 5% of ₦3,000, which is ₦2,850. Profit per carton is ₦2,850 − ₦2,500 = ₦350, so total gross profit is ₦350 × 400 = ₦140,000. Ignoring the trade discount gives ₦500 × 400 = ₦200,000, which overstates the profit.

questions.q: A trader in Jos bought a rechargeable lamp for ₦1,800 and sold it for ₦2,250. What is the mark-up on cost?
questions.explanation: The profit is ₦2,250 − ₦1,800 = ₦450. Mark-up on cost is profit divided by cost, so ₦450 ÷ ₦1,800 × 100 = 25%. Using selling price as the base gives 20%, which is the margin on selling price, not the mark-up on cost.

questions.q: Bello Transport Ltd charges ₦1,500 per tonne for the first 5 tonnes and ₦1,200 per tonne for every additional tonne. How much will it charge to move 12 tonnes of goods from Ilorin to Lagos?
questions.explanation: The first 5 tonnes cost 5 × ₦1,500 = ₦7,500. The remaining 7 tonnes cost 7 × ₦1,200 = ₦8,400, giving a total of ₦7,500 + ₦8,400 = ₦15,900. Charging all 12 tonnes at ₦1,500 gives ₦18,000, which ignores the lower rate for additional tonnes.

questions.q: A textile firm in Kano wishes to send the same detailed price list to 300 customers at minimum cost and retain a written record. Which communication method is most suitable?
questions.explanation: Electronic mail can send the same detailed written message to many customers at low cost and keeps a record of the message. A telephone conversation, courier delivery of separate letters, and a radio announcement do not combine wide simultaneous delivery, low cost, and a written record as well.

questions.q: Which Nigerian agency has the primary responsibility of setting and enforcing quality standards for manufactured goods such as electrical cables and cement?
options: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC)
National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)
questions.explanation: The Standards Organisation of Nigeria is mainly responsible for setting and enforcing standards for manufactured goods and industrial products. NAFDAC handles food, drugs, and related products, while the NCC regulates telecommunications and the FCCPC handles competition and general consumer protection matters.

questions.q: Umar bought a generator from a dealer in Sokoto who described it as 'in perfect working condition'. It developed a serious engine fault the following day due to a defect that existed before the sale. What is the most appropriate consumer remedy?
options: The buyer may claim repair, replacement or refund as appropriate.
The buyer automatically becomes entitled to double the purchase price.
The buyer must resell the generator and bear the loss.
The buyer can only complain if the manufacturer is in the same state.
questions.explanation: A buyer is entitled to redress when goods are defective or fail to match the description given by the seller. Depending on the circumstances, the remedy may be repair, replacement, or refund. There is no automatic right to double the purchase price, and the buyer is not required to resell the defective generator.

questions.q: Grace bought a sealed packet of biscuits in Enugu and found it contaminated with a harmful substance. Which consumer right is most directly violated?
questions.explanation: The right to safety protects consumers from goods that are hazardous or unfit for consumption. Contaminated biscuits directly endanger health. The right to be heard, the right to choose, and the right to consumer education concern other aspects of consumer protection.

questions.q: A trader in Kano supplied goods worth ₦180,000 to a customer in Kaduna. The customer later returned goods valued at ₦25,000 because they were of the wrong size. Which document should the seller issue to reduce the customer's debt?
questions.explanation: A credit note is issued to inform a buyer that an amount has been credited to the buyer's account, often because goods were returned or an overcharge occurred. A debit note would normally increase the amount owed, while a pro forma invoice is a preliminary invoice and a purchase order is the buyer's request to buy.

questions.q: A manufacturer in Kaduna sends goods by rail to a distributor in Ibadan. Which document travels with the goods and is signed by the distributor as evidence that the goods were received?
questions.explanation: A consignment note accompanies goods in transit and contains details of the goods and parties, and a signed copy can serve as evidence of delivery. A bill of exchange is a payment instrument, a credit note adjusts accounts for returns or overcharges, and a statement of account summarises transactions over a period.

questions.q: Ada, an individual in Aba, advertises her fairly used generator on an online classified platform, and Emeka, another individual in Owerri, pays her directly after seeing the advert. Which type of e-commerce is illustrated?
questions.explanation: The transaction is between two private individuals rather than a business selling to a final consumer. Business-to-business involves transactions between firms, while business-to-consumer involves a business selling directly to an individual customer.

questions.q: Kemi orders a sewing machine from an online store in Lagos. The store hands the parcel to a courier company for delivery to her home in Ibadan. The courier company is performing which e-commerce function?
questions.explanation: The courier moves the purchased goods from the seller to the buyer, which is part of order fulfilment and logistics. A payment gateway handles electronic payments, while online promotion creates awareness of products.

questions.q: A well-known detergent brand that has been on sale for many years runs short radio jingles mainly to remind consumers that it is still available. Which advertising objective is the firm pursuing?
questions.explanation: Reminder advertising keeps an established product in the minds of consumers and reinforces brand familiarity. Informative advertising is usually used to introduce a new product, while persuasive advertising tries to convince consumers to switch brands.

questions.q: A beauty shop in Lagos sends personalised text messages to customers who bought products last month, offering them 10% off their next purchase. This promotional activity is best described as:
questions.explanation: Direct marketing communicates with individual customers through channels such as text messages, email or phone calls to encourage a purchase. Public relations and publicity focus more on building goodwill or gaining unpaid public attention.

questions.q: A company sells its premium tea only through selected supermarkets and not through roadside kiosks. Which element of the marketing mix is being described?
questions.explanation: Place refers to the distribution channels and outlets used to make a product available to customers. The decision to use selected supermarkets rather than roadside kiosks is therefore a distribution decision.

questions.q: A factory in Benin City processes old tyres into floor tiles for sale. This activity is an example of:
questions.explanation: Secondary production involves transforming raw or used materials into finished or more useful goods, as in manufacturing floor tiles from old tyres. Primary production involves extraction, while tertiary production involves services.

questions.q: A broker in Cross River links cocoa farmers with foreign buyers and earns a commission from each sale. His occupation is best classified as:
questions.explanation: The broker provides a commercial service of linking buyers and sellers rather than extracting or manufacturing goods. Such services fall under tertiary occupations.

questions.q: Adebayo deposits ₦150,000 in a fixed deposit account that pays 8% simple interest per annum. What total amount will be in the account after 9 months?
questions.explanation: Interest = ₦150,000 × 8/100 × 9/12 = ₦9,000, so the total amount is ₦150,000 + ₦9,000 = ₦159,000. The figure ₦162,000 comes from using a full year instead of 9 months.

questions.q: Which of the following is a function of a commercial bank rather than the Central Bank of Nigeria?
options: Accepting deposits from members of the public
Acting as lender of last resort to banks
questions.explanation: Commercial banks accept deposits from customers and use such funds to grant loans and provide other banking services. Issuing legal tender currency, managing external reserves and acting as lender of last resort are central banking functions.

questions.q: Musa, an exporter in Kano, wants a bank in Dubai to guarantee that he will be paid after he presents shipping documents showing that the goods have been sent. Which document is suitable for this purpose?
questions.explanation: A letter of credit is a bank undertaking to pay the exporter when the required shipping documents are presented, reducing the risk of non-payment. A pro forma invoice is only a quotation or advance invoice, while a packing list describes the goods in a consignment.

questions.q: Chinwe buys 400 shares of a quoted company through a stockbroker at ₦22.50 per share. The broker charges 2% brokerage. What total amount does Chinwe pay, including brokerage?
questions.explanation: The cost of the shares is 400 × ₦22.50 = ₦9,000. Brokerage is 2% of ₦9,000 = ₦180, so the total paid is ₦9,000 + ₦180 = ₦9,180. The other amounts either ignore brokerage, use too high a brokerage rate, or deduct brokerage instead of adding it.

questions.q: In a limited partnership, the partner who contributes capital but does not take part in management and is liable only up to the capital contributed is known as a
questions.explanation: A limited partner contributes capital but does not manage the firm and has liability limited to the amount contributed. A general or active partner takes part in management and normally has unlimited liability.
